object.flags: does not cast shadow: the object has no shadow. transparent self-occlusion: its transparent parts hide each other (holographic look; in stock tags only Cortana uses it). brighter than it should be: boosts its ambient, light and reflection colors (stock weapons and powerups). not a pathfinding obstacle: AI paths ignore its pathfinding spheres. The other three flags don't exist in the original game.
object.bounding radius: Defines the approximate maximum size of an object. Used to optimize rendering, shadows, LOD, collisions, physics, spawning, interactions and AI pathfinding. It must fully contain the object without being too large or too small, as incorrect values can cause visual, collision and gameplay issues.
object.bounding offset: Center of the bounding sphere, from the root node (world units). Visibility, lighting and AI obstacle checks use this point, so place it at the middle of the model.
object.origin offset: Moves the whole model (nodes, markers and collision) away from the object's position, along the object's own axes (world units).
object.acceleration scale: Scales the acceleration of this object from forces like explosions, such as when weapons or powerups are moved by grenades. This does not apply to non-moving object types. If the scale is '0' then the item will not react.
object.model: Render model, with its nodes, markers and regions. Without one the object is invisible and has a single node.
object.animation graph: Animations played on the model's nodes. A vehicle's graph needs at least one element in UNITS: with none, the game crashes when it spawns.
object.collision model: What the object collides with: hit detection, damage and the pathfinding spheres AI avoids. Without one the object has no collision and takes no damage.
object.physics: The vehicle's physics tag. Only vehicles simulate it. On any object that has one, the object's position becomes its center of mass, which shifts the model.
object.modifier shader: Extra transparent shader drawn over the whole model, such as an energy shield. Its animation reads the object's functions and change colors. A plasma shader is not drawn while the function in its 'intensity source' is 0.
object.creation effect: Effect played once on the object when it is created.
object.render bounding radius: Radius of the sphere that decides whether the object is visible. If it is smaller than 'bounding radius', it is raised to that value when the tag loads. Set it for objects whose model reaches past the bounding radius, like the Pelican.
object.A in: Game value (0 to 1) that feeds input A, read by this object's functions and change colors. body / shield vitality: what is left. recent damage: damage just taken. random constant: one random value per object. region damage: damage of that model region. alive: 1, or 0 when dead. compass: heading from the level's north. The umbrella shield and shield stun options are not implemented. A unit, weapon or device with its own 'A in' set replaces this one.
object.B in: Game value (0 to 1) that feeds input B, read by this object's functions and change colors. body / shield vitality: what is left. recent damage: damage just taken. random constant: one random value per object. region damage: damage of that model region. alive: 1, or 0 when dead. compass: heading from the level's north. The umbrella shield and shield stun options are not implemented. A unit, weapon or device with its own 'B in' set replaces this one.
object.C in: Game value (0 to 1) that feeds input C, read by this object's functions and change colors. body / shield vitality: what is left. recent damage: damage just taken. random constant: one random value per object. region damage: damage of that model region. alive: 1, or 0 when dead. compass: heading from the level's north. The umbrella shield and shield stun options are not implemented. A unit, weapon or device with its own 'C in' set replaces this one.
object.D in: Game value (0 to 1) that feeds input D, read by this object's functions and change colors. body / shield vitality: what is left. recent damage: damage just taken. random constant: one random value per object. region damage: damage of that model region. alive: 1, or 0 when dead. compass: heading from the level's north. The umbrella shield and shield stun options are not implemented. A unit, weapon or device with its own 'D in' set replaces this one.
object.hud text message index: Index of the object's name in the 'alternate icon text' string list of the HUD globals. Shown in prompts such as picking up a weapon, swapping equipment or exiting a vehicle.
object.forced shader permutation index: When not 0, every shader of the model uses this permutation instead of its own. 0 = keep them. An actor variant can replace it.
object.attachments: Lights, looping sounds, effects, contrails and particle systems created with the object and attached to it.
object.attachments.type: What is attached. Light volumes are accepted here but the game doesn't create them: add them under widgets.
object.attachments.marker: Model marker it attaches to. Effects ignore this: they use the markers of their own locations.
object.attachments.primary scale: Object function (A to D out) that scales this attachment. none = full strength.
object.attachments.secondary scale: Second scale function. Only effects use it; the other attachment types ignore it.
object.attachments.change color: Object change color (A to D) that tints it. Lights, effects, contrails and particle systems use it; sounds ignore it.
object.widgets: Flags, antennas, glows, light volumes and lightning created with the object.
object.widgets.reference: The widget's tag. Where it attaches is set in that tag, by its marker.
object.functions: Up to 4 functions (A to D out) that turn inputs and time into animated values for shaders, attachments and change colors. They run from top to bottom: a function reads this tick's value of the ones above it and the last tick's of the ones below. Order of the math: function, scale function by, invert, wobble, square wave, steps, sawtooth, add, scale result by, map to, scale by, bounds.
object.functions.flags: invert: value becomes 1 - value, right after 'scale function by'. additive: every tick adds its result to the previous value and wraps at 1, so it keeps climbing. always active: stays on at or below the lower bound, where a function normally turns off.
object.functions.period: Seconds that scale the curve; 0 is read as 1. A cosine, diagonal wave or slide takes period x 1.43 seconds per full cycle. Each object starts at a different point of the curve.
object.functions.scale period by: Multiplies the period by this value, so lower values run faster. Ignored while the value is 0 or less.
object.functions.function: Curve from 0 to 1 over time. one / zero: constant. cosine: smooth wave. diagonal wave: straight up and down. slide: rises, then jumps back to 0. noise: random values. jitter / wander: the same irregular wave. spark: irregular rise with a sharp drop. (variable period): the same curve at an irregular speed.
object.functions.scale function by: Multiplies the curve by this value.
object.functions.wobble function: Curve of the wobble that is added to the value.
object.functions.wobble period: Speed of the wobble. Despite the 'seconds' in Guerilla, the game multiplies time by it, so higher = faster. A cosine takes 1.43 / this value seconds per full cycle.
object.functions.wobble magnitude: How far the wobble moves the value, up and down (0.1 = +/- 0.1). 0 = no wobble. Guerilla calls it percent, but it is a plain amount.
object.functions.square wave threshold: When not 0, values above it become 1 and the rest become 0.
object.functions.step count: Snaps the value to this many levels (5 = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1). 0 or 1 = off.
object.functions.map to: Curve applied to the result. linear: unchanged. early / very early: rises fast, then slows. late / very late: rises slowly, then fast. cosine: soft start and end.
object.functions.sawtooth count: Cuts the value into teeth that repeat every 1 / (count - 1). They are not rescaled: with 5, each tooth only goes from 0 to 0.25. 0 or 1 = off.
object.functions.add: Adds this value to the result, up to a maximum of 1.
object.functions.scale result by: Multiplies the result by this value.
object.functions.bounds mode: clip: keeps the result inside the bounds. clip and normalize: the same, then remaps the bounds to 0-1. scale to fit: remaps 0-1 to the bounds.
object.functions.bounds: Lower and upper limit; equal values are read as 0 to 1. At or below the lower bound the function turns off, unless it is 'always active'.
object.functions.turn off with: Index of another function (0 = A, 1 = B, 2 = C, 3 = D; -1 = none). While that function is off, this one is off too.
object.functions.scale by: Multiplies the value just before the bounds. 0 = ignored.
object.functions.usage: Free note about what this function is for. The game doesn't read it.
object.change colors: Up to 4 colors (A to D) that the object's shaders and attachments can use. Each is picked from its permutations when the object is created, or driven by a function with 'scale by'.
object.change colors.darken by: Multiplies the color by this value. Set 'scale by' too: the game only recalculates colors when a change color uses it.
object.change colors.scale by: Value that blends between the lower (0) and upper (1) color every tick. none = the color stays as it was picked at creation.
object.change colors.scale flags: blend in hsv: blends through hue instead of mixing RGB, taking the shortest way around the color wheel. ...more colors: takes the long way around instead, passing through more colors.
object.change colors.color lower bound: Color when 'scale by' is 0. Not used without 'scale by'.
object.change colors.color upper bound: Color when 'scale by' is 1. Not used without 'scale by'.
object.change colors.permutations: Colors to choose from when the object is created. The choice depends on the object's position, so an object placed in the same spot always gets the same color.
object.change colors.permutations.weight: Chance of this permutation relative to the others (1, 1, 2 = 25%, 25%, 50%). All 0 = equal chance.
object.change colors.permutations.color: One end of this permutation's color range. The final color falls between both ends, depending on the object's position.
Other end of this permutation's color range. The final color falls between both ends, depending on the object's position.
object.predicted resources: Bitmaps and sounds the game loads ahead of time so the object doesn't stutter when it appears. Stock tag files leave it empty; it is built with the map.
object.predicted resources.type: Whether the resource is a bitmap or a sound.
object.predicted resources.resource inde: Which bitmap inside the bitmap tag.
object.predicted resources.tag index: Index of the bitmap or sound tag inside the built map.
physics.radius: Positive: old physics (inertia from the mass points and 'moment scale', no sweep against the level, other vehicles don't push it). Zero or negative: new physics (uses the inertial matrix, mass points can't pass through walls). Stock vehicles use -1.
physics.moment scale: Multiplies the whole inertia (old and new physics). Higher = harder to spin.
physics.mass: Total mass. Gravity, ground spring, drive and antigrav all scale with it, so alone it does not change how the vehicle moves. It matters when vehicles collide (heavier pushes lighter) and for impulses. Above 7500 the ground material's friction scale is ignored.
physics.center of mass: Mass-weighted average of the mass point positions. Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter. The vehicle rotates around this point.
physics.density: Average density. With each mass point's relative density it decides buoyancy: a mass point floats when its density is lower than 'water density'.
physics.gravity scale: Multiplies gravity (0.003565 world units per tick squared). 1 = normal, 0 = weightless. The ground spring always uses normal gravity.
physics.ground friction: Part of the sliding speed each grounded mass point removes per tick, by its share of the mass (drag, not dry friction). 0 = ice, 1 = stops at once. Wheels and treads push through this same value, so 0 also means no traction. Multiplied by the ground material's scale when mass <= 7500.
physics.ground depth: How deep one mass point sinks when it carries the whole weight (ground spring: force = weight x depth / ground depth). Smaller = stiffer ground contact.
physics.ground damp fraction: Damping of the ground spring: part of the speed into the ground each grounded mass point cancels per tick. Low = bouncy, high = lands dead.
physics.ground normal k1: Slope limit for wheels / treads: full traction when the ground normal's Z is at least k1 (0.707 = 45 degrees), none at k0.
physics.ground normal k0: Slope limit for wheels / treads: no traction when the ground normal's Z is k0 or less (0.5 = 60 degrees), full at k1.
physics.water friction: Like air friction, for mass points under water: part of their speed removed per tick, by their share of the mass.
physics.water depth: Depth under water where a mass point gets full buoyancy and water lift. 0 = no buoyancy.
physics.water density: Density of water for buoyancy. A mass point floats when its own density is lower.
physics.air friction: Part of the speed every mass point loses per tick, always, by its share of the mass. Sets the top speed in free fall and how fast spinning stops in the air.
physics.xx moment: Inertia around the x axis: sum of mass x moment scale x distance squared to the axis (+ 0.4 x radius squared with new physics). Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter. Boats, alien scouts and alien fighters scale their steering torque with the moments.
physics.yy moment: Inertia around the y axis: sum of mass x moment scale x distance squared to the axis (+ 0.4 x radius squared with new physics). Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter. Boats, alien scouts and alien fighters scale their steering torque with the moments.
physics.zz moment: Inertia around the z axis: sum of mass x moment scale x distance squared to the axis (+ 0.4 x radius squared with new physics). Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter. Boats, alien scouts and alien fighters scale their steering torque with the moments.
physics.inertial matrix and inverse: Full inertia matrix and its inverse. Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter. New physics (radius <= 0) turns torque into rotation with the inverse.
physics.powered mass points: What the vehicle drives. The vehicle type uses them by INDEX and needs an exact count: human jeep 2 (0 and 1 steer in opposite directions: front, back), human tank 2 (0 = left tread, 1 = right tread), human boat 3, alien fighter 2, alien scout any (all hover). With another count nothing is powered. Turrets and human planes never use them.
physics.powered mass points.flags: What the mass points using this one do. ground / water / air friction: push along their forward at the vehicle's speed (wheels and treads = ground friction). water / air lift: force along their up, by forward speed. thrust: force along forward. antigrav: hover.
physics.powered mass points.antigrav str: Hover force of each mass point at ground level, as a multiple of the vehicle's weight. The points together need more than 1 to lift it.
physics.powered mass points.antigrav hei: Height over the ground where the hover force ends. It grows as (1 - height / antigrav height) squared.
physics.powered mass points.antigrav dam: Damping of the hover: how much of the speed towards the ground is cancelled per tick. Low = bobs up and down.
physics.powered mass points.antigrav nor: Full hover force when the mass point's up Z is at least k1; none at k0 (tilted vehicles lose lift).
No hover force when the mass point's up Z is k0 or less; full at k1.
physics.mass points: Spheres that touch the level and other vehicles; every force acts at their centers. At least 3 must be on the ground for the vehicle to come to rest. Up to 32.
physics.mass points.role: Toolkit shortcut, not a tag field: the role itself is not saved in the tag. Picking one (front tire, tread, wing...) fills this mass point's powered mass point, metallic flag, relative density and friction with the values stock vehicles use for that part. It only lists roles this tag can use. Custom = the current values match no role.
physics.mass points.powered mass point: Index of the powered mass point that drives this one; -1 = none.
physics.mass points.model node: Node of the model the sphere was linked to in the JMS; tool writes it. The game does not read it: mass points stay where they are in the default pose, they don't follow animated nodes.
physics.mass points.flags: metallic: slipping on the ground plays the vehicle material effects' 'vehicle chassis slip' effect instead of 'vehicle tire slip' (scraping instead of a tire).
physics.mass points.relative mass: Share of the total mass: mass x relative / sum of all relatives. Heavier points get more friction and pull the center of mass towards them.
physics.mass points.mass: Total mass x relative mass / sum of all relative masses. Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter.
physics.mass points.relative density: Density relative to the other mass points, for buoyancy. Lower = floats more.
physics.mass points.density: Tag density x relative density x sum(relative mass / relative density) / sum(relative mass). Recalculated by tool, Guerilla and Sapien every time they load the tag, so its value in the file does not matter.
physics.mass points.position: Center of the sphere, from the object's origin (world units).
physics.mass points.forward: Direction wheels / treads / thrust push in, and the axis of 'forward' friction. Steering turns it.
physics.mass points.up: Direction of lift forces and the axis of 'up' friction. Wheels only grip when it points along the ground normal.
physics.mass points.friction type: point: same friction every way. forward / left / up: friction along that axis x parallel scale, across it x perpendicular scale. A wheel is 'forward' with low parallel (rolls) and high perpendicular (grips sideways).
physics.mass points.friction parallel sc: Multiplies friction along the friction type's axis (not used by 'point').
physics.mass points.friction perpendicul: Multiplies friction across the friction type's axis (not used by 'point').
physics.mass points.radius: Radius of the sphere (world units): contact with the ground and other vehicles' mass points.
